chunks: And from him, from Safwan and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the camel (badanah), how should it be sheared (ushir)? He said: 'While it is kneeling (barikah), slaughter it while it is standing, and shear it from its right side. Then it enters the state of Ihram when it is adorned (qillad) and sheared.'

key_terms.الْبَدَنَةِ: The female camel used for sacrifice in Hajj
key_terms.قُلِّدَتْ: Adorned with a collar (qilad) typically placed on the neck
key_terms.يُحْرِمُ: Enters the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)
key_terms.يُشْعِرُهَا: To shear or cut the hair of the animal

ai.seo_question: How is a camel prepared and slaughtered for Hajj according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), transmitted via the reliable chain of Safwan and Ibn Abi Umayr, specifies the precise ritual mechanics for the *badanah* (sacrificial camel) in Hajj al-Qiran or al-Tamattu'. It highlights the Sunnah of slaughtering the animal while standing and shearing from the right side, a practice that underscores the physical ease and ritual purity required before assuming the state of Ihram.
